study type: Exploratory post hoc analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: Periconceptional BMI change (categorized into quartiles of weight loss/gain)
cohort: The study included 244 obese infertile women who achieved an ongoing pregnancy within 24 months after randomization in the LIFEstyle study.
finding: A periconceptional decrease in BMI in obese infertile women was associated with a decrease in the rates of hypertensive pregnancy complications and preterm birth.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in rates of spontaneous vaginal birth or Caesarean section across different periconceptional BMI change quartiles.
